title: Nvidia Earnings Loom, Bitcoin Holds $64K, Deutsche Bank Leaks Hit
description:
Wall Street tumbles ahead of Nvidia's first earnings report without Jensen Huang, with options implying a $335B swing. Bitcoin holds key support at $64,994 while precious metals battle paper market liquidations. Meanwhile, a 15-million-file leak triggers a $4.2 billion market cap drop for Deutsche Bank.

Featuring analysis inspired by Jason Pizzino, Michael Pizzino, Financial Education 2, and MindTheChart.

segments.heading: Nvidia Earnings & Market Turbulence
segments.narration: Nvidia prepares to publish its first earnings report without Jensen Huang at the helm. Options pricing signals a massive $335 billion market value swing while global tech stocks slide. Meanwhile, Bitcoin fights to hold critical support near $64,994, and a 15-million-file leak triggers a multibillion-dollar bank sell-off.
bullets: European banking shares slip on leaks

segments.heading: Wall Street Sells Off
segments.narration: Wall Street indexes face intense selling pressure ahead of key corporate reports. The S&P 500 fell 1.9% to 7,417 points. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite recorded the steepest decline, dropping 2.5% to 24,510 points. The Dow Jones lost 1.4%, closing at 51,608 points. Volatility is rising quickly, with the VIX holding near 23 points after gaining 17% over five days. Fixed income markets remain tight as the US 10-year yield sits at 5.1%. European equities are also under pressure, with the Euro Stoxx 50 down 0.9% to 6,288 and the FTSE MIB down 0.6% to 51,218. In commodities, gold trades at $3,862 per ounce while WTI crude oil edges up to $86 per barrel.

segments.heading: Nvidia Earnings Post-Huang Era
segments.narration: Nvidia faces an unprecedented test with its upcoming quarterly results following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang. Options activity points to a historic $335 billion potential swing in market cap after earnings. Regulatory headwinds are intensifying. Federal agencies opened formal investigations into key server partner Megaspeed back in 2024 over international hardware transfers. At the same time, expanding US export controls on artificial intelligence hardware continue to create operational friction across global supply chains. Nvidia stock is severely oversold, having dropped 28% over the past month. Sell-offs are cascading through the entire tech space. Sandisk shares have fallen nearly 40% in a month, while CoreWeave has plunged 54% over the last three months. High system-wide margin debt is accelerating forced selling across high-growth AI equities.

segments.heading: Bitcoin Battles Key Support
segments.narration: Bitcoin is holding near $64,994 after breaking an eleven-day series of lower daily highs. The digital asset has lost roughly 30% over the past two months, slicing through major technical support levels at $75,000, $71,000, and $67,000. Historical bear cycles show that up to 63% of weekly candles tend to close red during extended drawdowns, pointing to prolonged consolidation before any sustained recovery. However, institutional buyers are stepping in at current lows. Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows have halted, with major institutional allocations doubling to $2.35 billion at Wells Fargo. As long as Bitcoin remains above its July structural low, immediate downside tests toward $50,000 are held at bay, though macro headwinds from a strong US dollar persist.

segments.heading: Gold and Silver Paper Crash
segments.narration: Precious metals are experiencing their sharpest downturn in years. Gold trades near $3,862 per ounce, down 32% from its January high. Silver has suffered an even deeper collapse, dropping 61% from its peak. This heightened volatility highlights structural vulnerabilities in paper trading. Derivatives markets for precious metals are estimated to be up to 400 times larger than the physical market, magnifying speculative liquidations during broad market pullbacks. Gold remains capped below its major breakdown zone of $3,900 per ounce, while the US Dollar Index exerts constant downward force across the metals space. Without a decisive breakout back above $3,900, potential downside support zones between $3,200 and $3,600 remain key focus areas.

segments.heading: Deutsche Bank Leaks Hit Banking
segments.narration: European banking shares hit sharp headwinds after a massive leak of 15 million internal files exposed major compliance failures. The documents reveal unchecked control breakdowns, high-risk Russian investments, and questionable payment routing. Deutsche Bank suffered a $4.2 billion market capitalization loss following the reports. The fallout pushed the Euro Stoxx 50 down 0.9% to 6,288 points, while Italy's FTSE MIB dropped 0.6% to 51,218 points. Banking equities face immediate sentiment drag as investors weigh potential regulatory penalties and stricter capital reserve demands. Meanwhile, data center policy disputes in European battlegrounds like Spain threaten to derail billions of dollars in technology infrastructure deals, creating broader market uncertainty across the region.

segments.heading: Upcoming Market Catalysts
segments.narration: Crucial economic data and policy events will dictate price action later this week. On Tuesday at 08:30 Eastern Time, the US releases Retail Sales data, with core sales expected at 0.4%. On Wednesday at 14:00 Eastern Time, the Federal Reserve publishes the FOMC meeting minutes, providing key insights into future rate decisions. On Thursday at 08:30 Eastern Time, markets will digest the Philly Fed Manufacturing Index alongside weekly Unemployment Claims, forecasted at 199K. In central bank communications, the European Central Bank presents its Financial Stability Review alongside scheduled executive addresses. Finally, trading in Anthropic shares begins on November 19.
bullets: US Retail Sales due Tuesday 08:30 ET

segments.heading: AI Agents Threaten Bank Runs
segments.narration: Financial stability faces potential threats from unexpected technological sources. Autonomous AI trading agents introduce unprecedented liquidity risks, with potential high-frequency withdrawals capable of triggering systemic bank runs in minutes.
bullets: Autonomous AI agents pose run risks
